title: Square up a racked gantry beam, then pull it in by both ends to its marks
instruction: The grey gantry beam rides between two guide rails and is out of square: its right end is 8 mm farther from you than its left end. First pull the right end toward you until the beam is square, then pull the beam toward you by both ends together until both ends are level with the yellow marks beside the rails. Never let one end lead the other by more than 12 mm, or the beam racks and jams. Then let go of it.
context: Gantry robots, CNC routers, 3D printers and the lab-automation rigs that run experiments for AI-driven research all move on a beam riding two parallel guides, and building and servicing them is hands-on work. Pulled or pushed from one end, a gantry racks: one end leads, the beam turns and its end bearings bind, the 'sticky drawer' effect of a wide, shallow carriage moved off-centre. Technicians moving an unpowered gantry for setup or maintenance read which end lags, square it first, then move both ends together (O*NET 17-3024.01 Robotics Technicians, 49-9044.00 Millwrights). Here neither arm, gripping straight down, reaches the far end of the beam; the beam must move with a gripper at each end, and the score follows the lead between the ends over the whole move, so the lagging end must be read and moved first, then the arms must move in step.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Guide rails: two fixed dark grey steel bars, 330 mm long (along x), 12 mm wide and 40 mm tall, running from x 17.0 to 50.0 cm, their inner faces at y +26.05 cm and -26.05 cm (521 mm apart). (2) Retaining lips: a fixed steel strip 10 mm wide and 6 mm thick along the top of each rail's inner face, its whole length, overhanging the gap by 10 mm with its underside 34 mm above the table, so the beam cannot be lifted out from between the rails. (3) Gantry beam: a loose hollow aluminium extrusion, 40 mm deep (along x), 520 mm long (along y) and 30 mm tall, 0.25 kg, lying flat on the table between the rails, its centre at x 44.4 cm, y 0, turned 0.88 degrees about the vertical so that the centre of its left end face is at x 44.0 cm and that of its right end face at x 44.8 cm (the right end 8 mm farther from the arms). Its ends sit under the lips, 4 mm below them; square, each end has 0.5 mm of play to its rail, and turned 1.8 degrees (a 16 mm lead) it touches both rails at diagonally opposite corners and binds. (4) Target marks: two thin yellow plastic tabs, 30 mm (along x) by 20 mm and 1 mm thick, fixed on the table just outside the rails, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +28.5 cm and -28.5 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the beam's pose and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). 'Lead' is how much farther from the arms (along x) the centre of one end face is than the other's; it starts at 8 mm. The beam is 'squared' at the first step its lead is 2 mm or less, and 'squared first' if by then its centre had moved no more than 25 mm toward the marks. 'Popped up' means the beam's lowest point is more than 5 mm above the table (the lips allow 4 mm) or its broad faces are tilted more than 5 degrees from level; 'off the rails' means an end face's centre is past either end of the rails or the beam's centre is more than 10 mm to one side of y 0. Each gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the current finger gap plus the 8 mm finger thickness, and half the fingers' 27 mm width across; 57 mm fully open); 'hands off' means both finger zones are at least 30 mm from the beam. A gripper is 'at an end' when its finger-tip point is within 10 mm of the beam and at least 130 mm from the beam's middle along its length, toward that end. Score 0 if at any step the lead is over 12 mm or the beam pops up or goes off the rails; if, on steps without a gripper at each end, its centre has come more than 20 mm toward the marks in all (net); or if it is never squared. Otherwise: 1.0 if both end faces' centres are within 5 mm of x 22.0 cm (level with the marks), the lead is 2 mm or less, the beam was squared first and its lead was never over 4 mm from then on, and hands are off; 0.75 if both end faces' centres are within 10 mm of x 22.0 cm, the beam was squared first and its lead was never over 7 mm from then on (the grippers may still hold it); 0.5 if the beam's centre is within 15 mm of x 22.0 cm; 0.25 if its centre has moved at least 30% of the way from its start to x 22.0 cm (67 mm); 0 in every other case (not squared, not moved far enough). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the beam still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'hands off' and 'a gripper at each end' are taken as met. In a real trial, a top video against 1 mm scales on both rails' tops gives the lead and where the grippers are, frame by frame, and a tape from each rail's near end gives the end positions.
fidelity: A plain beam between two fixed guide rails stands in for a gantry on linear guides (no rollers, bearings or motors); about 1:3 scale. Rigid bodies; every object has the simulator's default rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic; the table keeps the scene's own material), so the beam drags and binds sooner than a lubricated guide; whether it locks is left to the physics engine, and the 12 mm limit is scored either way. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Put the beam back flat between the rails at the back, centred at x 44.4 cm, y 0, with the centre of its left end face at x 44.0 cm and that of its right end face at x 44.8 cm (the right end lagging 8 mm). Nothing is consumed.
